name: PrestaShop
title: PrestaShop SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on PrestaShop’s webservice API: 24 of 43 services wired. Browsing and cart work; no shopper sign-in, and the storefront cannot place orders.
lede: The PrestaShop connector works through the webservice API, and that API is the constraint: it has no customer login and no cart-to-order checkout. Browsing and the cart are wired; placing an order is not possible through it.
verdict: Shoppers can browse and fill a cart, but cannot sign in or place an order. Checkout counts as wired because the list of carriers comes from PrestaShop; the webservice API has no checkout or payment surface — placing an order is something only a front-office payment module can do — so every way the storefront places an order, cash on delivery included, is a placeholder.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your PrestaShop shop

env.name: PUBLIC_PRESTASHOP_API_URL
env.note: Your PrestaShop shop’s URL. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_PRESTASHOP_API_KEY
env.note: The webservice key from Advanced Parameters › Webservice. Every call needs it. See the limitations.

env.name: PUBLIC_PRESTASHOP_LANGUAGE_ID
env.note: The shop’s language ID, sent as `language=<id>` so translatable fields come back as plain values rather than per-language arrays.

env.name: PUBLIC_PRESTASHOP_SHOP_ID
env.note: Multistore shop ID (`id_shop`). Falls back to `PUBLIC_PRESTASHOP_STORE_ID` when unset.

env.name: PUBLIC_PRESTASHOP_STORE_ID
env.note: Read as the shop ID when `PUBLIC_PRESTASHOP_SHOP_ID` is unset.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/prestashop-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: `init.ts` hands the connector every `PUBLIC_PRESTASHOP_*` variable that is set, camel-cased. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_PRESTASHOP_API_SECRET`, `PUBLIC_PRESTASHOP_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `PUBLIC_PRESTASHOP_ACCESS_KEY` and `PUBLIC_PRESTASHOP_CHANNEL_ID`; the connector’s source does not read them.
backendSettings: Enable the webservice and create a key under Advanced Parameters › Webservice, with access to the resources the storefront reads — and read the limitations first.
howItWorks: The webservice API is PrestaShop’s back-office API, not a storefront one: it has no customer login and no cart-to-order flow. The connector reads the catalogue and manages carts through it, and lists the shop’s active carriers as shipping options — without prices, because PrestaShop computes those outside the webservice.
Writes need care: translatable fields must be sent with `<language>` children, and echoing a `display=full` read straight back silently blanks them — a bug the connector hit and fixed.
limitations: The storefront cannot place an order. The webservice API has no checkout and no payment resource; placing an order is `PaymentModule::validateOrder()`, which only a front-office payment module can call. So cash on delivery, Razorpay, Stripe and every other way the storefront places an order are placeholders on PrestaShop.
Shipping options come without prices: PrestaShop works them out from delivery ranges, zones and modules outside the webservice API.

The webservice key the connector sends on every call comes from `PUBLIC_PRESTASHOP_API_KEY`. SvelteKit sends `PUBLIC_` variables to the browser, so every visitor to the store can read it and use whatever permissions the key has.

faq.q: Can I run a PrestaShop store on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: No. Shoppers can browse and fill a cart, but the webservice API has no shopper sign-in and no way to place an order — only a front-office payment module can do that — so every checkout path in the storefront is a placeholder.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to PrestaShop?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/prestashop-connector`, set `PUBLIC_PRESTASHOP_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: Why can’t shoppers sign in on PrestaShop?
faq.a: The webservice API has no customer login endpoint, so the connector’s `auth` throws rather than fake a session. The Svelte Commerce maintainers have asked PrestaShop’s maintainers whether a supported storefront sign-in path exists over the webservice API.

openQuestion: Is there a supported storefront auth path over the webservice API?

api.surface: The connector calls PrestaShop’s REST webservice through its single `/api` gateway, forcing JSON responses with the `Output-Format: JSON` and `Io-Format: JSON` headers and sending every write as an XML body with `Content-Type: text/xml`, because the webservice reads no JSON input.
api.auth: Every request carries HTTP Basic auth with the webservice key as the username and an empty password, which authenticates the shop rather than a shopper; there is no session or token to refresh, and shopper sign-in is not possible, so every `auth` method that would establish an identity throws `NotSupportedError`.

calls.what: `GET /api/products` with `display=full`, `filter[active]=[1]`, `limit=offset,count` and `sort=[col_DIR]`; a slug read is `filter[link_rewrite]=[slug]`, completed by `GET /api/combinations`, `/api/product_option_values`, `/api/product_options` and `/api/stock_availables`
`POST /api/carts` with `id_lang` and `id_currency`; `GET /api/carts/{id}?display=full`; `PUT /api/carts/{id}` with the whole record; `DELETE /api/carts/{id}`

rules: PrestaShop has no count route, no pagination envelope and no total header, so the connector pages with `limit=offset,count` from a 0-based offset and takes the total from a second request with the same filters and no limit, counting the ids it returns.
Sorting is sent as `sort=[date_add_DESC]` and similar, and a sort on `date_add` or `date_upd` also sends `date=1`, without which PrestaShop ignores it.

`/api/search` returns bare product ids and answers 400 without `language`, so search is two requests, the second a `filter[id]=[a|b|c]` list capped at 600 ids to keep the URL under the default 8 KB request-line limit.

A cart record carries no totals, so the connector computes them from catalogue prices as a tax-excluded estimate, and every cart change is a `PUT` of the whole record with `associations.cart_rows` as a complete set; the cart id is kept in `localStorage` under `cart_id`.

The webservice key identifies the application, not a shopper, so `GET /api/orders` with no filter returns every order in the shop; the order list is scoped to one customer only when the caller passes `customerId`, sent as `filter[id_customer]`.
